theme: Unit 1 review, Creation & the Covenant of Works
memoryText: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Today there is no new reading. Today is for review and reflection on what you have learned in Unit 1.

Begin by memorizing the verse above if you have not already. Genesis 1:1 is the foundational sentence of the entire Bible. Everything that follows, every covenant, every promise, every doctrine, rests on the claim it makes. There is a God. He created. He made the heavens and the earth. Before any biblical doctrine can be constructed, this single verse must be settled.

Say it aloud several times today, slowly. Notice each phrase. “In the beginning”, there was a beginning, and God was there. “God created”, not chaos, not gods, not accidents. God. “The heavens and the earth”, everything that is, in every realm, from every angle, all of it. This one verse refutes atheism (God exists), polytheism (one God), pantheism (God is distinct from creation), dualism (one source, not two), and naturalism (the universe is not self-existent). All of it, in seven English words.

Carry this verse with you through the day. Repeat it when you encounter something beautiful in creation. Repeat it when something feels chaotic. Repeat it when you doubt the goodness of the world. The God who began everything is the God who oversees everything still.
unitRecap:
In Unit 1 you have traveled through the first three chapters of Genesis and met the foundational doctrines on which the entire Christian faith rests. The unit began with creation itself, the God who speaks, the world he ordered, the humanity he crowned with glory and honor. You then descended into Genesis 3, where the rebellion of humanity broke what God had made good, and yet, even in that chapter, the first promise of a Redeemer was spoken.

Along the way, the plan paused three times for doctrinal reflection: on the Bible itself, the foundation of everything else; on the image of God, the basis of human dignity; and on the doctrine of sin, the diagnosis of what is wrong with the world and with each of us.

The Psalms then taught us how to respond to what we had learned. Psalm 8 marveled at the dignity God has given humanity. Psalm 104 led us through creation as ongoing providence. Psalm 19 listened to the wordless witness of the heavens. Psalm 33 contemplated the power of God’s word. Psalm 29 thundered with the majesty of his voice. And Psalm 65 brought together creation, atonement, and joy in a single song.

This first unit has done foundational work. You have met the God of the Bible, Creator, holy, sovereign, near. You have met humanity as it was meant to be, image-bearing, dignified, in covenant. You have met sin, universal, deep, devastating. And you have heard the first whisper of grace, the offspring of the woman who would crush the serpent’s head. Everything that comes next in the Bible builds on this foundation. The unit you are completing is the soil out of which the rest of the story grows.

reviewQuestions.question: What does the order and goodness of creation reveal about God’s character?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Think about what Genesis 1 shows us through its pattern and rhythm. Creation is ordered, not chaotic, speaking to God’s mind. It is good, not neutral, speaking to God’s character. It is given as gift to image-bearers, speaking to God’s generosity. Sit with this question: if you knew nothing about God except what Genesis 1 reveals, what would you conclude about him? Write a few sentences in your own words.

reviewQuestions.question: What was the nature of the covenant God made with Adam in the garden?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Revisit Genesis 2. God provided abundantly (“of every tree you may surely eat”), placed one prohibition, and made it a test of trust. This is sometimes called the covenant of works. What were the terms? What was at stake? And what does the structure tell you about the pattern of all true relationship with God, gift before command, grace before obedience?

reviewQuestions.question: What did the Fall change about the relationship between God and humanity?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Walk through Genesis 3 in your memory. What broke between God and Adam and Eve? What broke between Adam and Eve themselves? What broke between humanity and creation? What broke inside the human heart? The Fall was not just one bad decision; it was a comprehensive shattering. Identify three specific things that changed.

reviewQuestions.question: Where is the first promise of redemption in Scripture, and what does it tell us?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Genesis 3:15, sometimes called the protoevangelium, the first gospel. Read it again. What does it promise? Who is the “offspring of the woman”? What does it cost him, and what does he accomplish? And how does this single verse plant the seed of everything that will follow in Scripture? Pray through this verse, thanking God that he did not abandon humanity even in the moment of our rebellion.

prayerPrompts: Thank God for what you have learned about him in these first weeks, naming one truth you want to keep.
Confess where you still resist what you have read, and ask him to keep working.
Ask him to anchor your life in the unit verse.
